data.title: Wifi Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2020 has a new wireless firmware which can support a high range of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone SE 2020. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone SE 2020 Wi-Fi issues are...

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone SE(2).
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone SE(2) are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone SE(2)’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.

Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.

Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.

Restore the default network connection

( Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone SE(2), you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone SE 2020 is not a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. Which means it can not resist dust and water coming in up to it. However, it can resist certain levels of water. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Network Problem
data.description:
The iPhone SE 2020 comes with upgraded network connectivity than the previous iPhone models and supports 4G network connectivity. Despite these technological advancements from the previous iPhone models, users have reported issues regarding the iPhone SE 2020 network connectivity. Such as loss in the network, prompt disconnections, inability to find or locate the network.

The most common issues however are often discussed upon Apple’s user forum and the most common problems found regarding network in iPhone SE(2) are:

  • iPhone SE(2) gets down to 0 network bars randomly
  • Network quality drops from 4G to 2G/3G.
  • Cannot access metered/Cellular internet connection through Carrier or the SIM Company.
  • Network never reaches the full level.

These common issues however can be a network receptor hardware glitch of the iPhone SE(2). To resolve these Apple recommends its iPhone SE(2) users some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes as a home remedy, such as:

Toggle Airplane Mode on and off to reset the previous network settings and cache.

Remove your sim card and reinstall it again. (requires a restart of the device)

Set up the internet for your phone if you’re facing internet issues through the network for the first time.

To set up go to Settings > Mobile Data > Mobile Data Network

then:

Insert APN (Access Point Name) provided by your carrier 

Insert Username (provided by your carrier)

Insert Password (provided by your carrier)

Save the settings by pressing the left arrow at the top.

Make sure your Data connection is on after setting up the network before you access the internet.

Install carrier update for your iPhone (Check-in Settings > General > About)

Restart your iPhone

Soft reset your iPhone

If none of the solutions work for your iPhone, you might need your phone to get checked by a professional technician. Here at ifixit bd, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in resolving your network issues in your iPhone SE 2020. ifixit bd has 4 service points which are located in points around Dhaka, Bangladesh.

  • Update your iOS Software.

  • Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from iStore.
  • Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help

data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy. They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

If the update still fails try updating from another pc.

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

The whole error code list: https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201444

However, not all problems can be fixed only by DIY fixes. Some errors might require some handy work around the inner parts of the phone which should be done by a professional iPhone technician. That is where ifixit bd comes in, we have dedicated and experienced technicians who specialize in repairing and resolving errors in iPhone SE(2) or any other iPhone devices. ifixit bd is a prominent Apple gadget servicing center based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. data.title: Housing Replacement
data.description:
The iPhone SE 2020 is a pretty sturdy phone considering an Aluminum body in the back. However, maybe through sheer bad luck, your phone can face some catastrophic damage which may damage your iPhone. One of the most common damages in phones are cosmetic damages, such as Display glass, or the back part. But sometimes your housing of the iPhone SE(2) may get damaged. Considering it has attained some serious damage. There’s a point to be cleared out, the housing of the iPhone should not be confused with the back-glass replacement of the iPhone SE(2).

So, if you, somehow, have managed to get your back part (housing) damaged. Damages of the housing may include.

  • The housing of the iPhone SE(2) bent, stressed
  • Deformation of the housing
  • Housing breaking into pieces
  • Visible scratches and dent
  • Loosening of the adhesive that holds the housing

Any sort of damage or deformation on the back housing of the iPhone SE(2) indicates that it might lead to an internal issue in the future. data.description:
Apple has introduced an exclusive feature of Touch ID since the iPhone 5s. It is a fingerprint sensor that lets users of the iPhone SE- 2020 unlock their iPhone without having to put in a passcode every time they do so. You are asked to enter the passcode to unlock the phone by default instead of Touch ID

Can’t Register Touch ID to set up your fingerprint.

Touch ID is grayed or dimmed out.

Apple recommends some fixes you may try in your home which may fix the issue if it is due to a software glitch. Those fixes are:

Make sure your hands are clean and dry. Different sorts of moisturizers may affect the workability of your iPhone. (Such as Oil, lotion, sweat, or water)

Make sure your iPhone touch ID is clean and wipe it down with a lint-free cloth.

Make sure you put your entire finger on the home button to make the sensor work.

Make sure your screen protector or case is not getting in the way of touch ID

Update your iOS

Also, make sure that Touch ID does not work if you have...

Restarted your phone

You haven’t unlocked your device in 48 hours

5 failed attempts to unlock the phone through touch ID.

The Taptic Engine in an iPhone Se 2020 is responsible for providing haptic feedback, such as vibrations for notifications and the "click" sensation for the home button (on supported models). You might need to replace the Taptic Engine in your iPhone if you experience any of the following issues:

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.
